Implement an event-driven system where the 'bike registered' event triggers the removal of the bike from the available list, ensuring immediate update across services. (Event Driven Architecture) A software architecture pattern promoting the production, detection, consumption, and reaction to events, enabling decoupled and scalable systems.

Use observer pattern within the application components to update the available bikes list upon bike registration. (Observer) A behavioral design pattern where an object (subject) maintains a list of dependents (observers) and notifies them automatically of any state changes.

Implement a proximity filter component that queries bike locations and returns only those within the user-specified radius (e.g., 100 meters). (Proximity Filter) A pattern that filters data based on spatial proximity criteria, allowing users to see only items within a specified distance.

Use a location-based service to manage bike location data and respond to proximity queries from users. (Location Based Service) A service that provides location-aware functionalities, such as finding nearby resources or services based on user location.

Implement payment methods as separate strategy classes (e.g., BankAccountPaymentStrategy, CardPaymentStrategy) that the payment context selects based on user choice. (Strategy) Defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable. Strategy lets the algorithm vary independently from clients that use it.

Use adapters to wrap external payment provider APIs to a common interface used by the system. (Adapter) Converts the interface of a class into another interface clients expect. Adapter lets classes work together that couldn't otherwise because of incompatible interfaces.

Create a payment facade that exposes simple methods for payment processing, internally delegating to appropriate payment method implementations. (Facade) Provides a unified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem. Facade defines a higher-level interface that makes the subsystem easier to use.

Implement a verification code generation and delivery system that sets the code validity to 30 minutes but expires the code if not entered within 30 seconds after sending. (Verification Code) A pattern where a code is generated and sent to the user via SMS or email to verify identity or action, with a validity period and expiration rules.

Use timeout to expire the verification code if not entered within 30 seconds. (Timeout) A pattern that invalidates a process or data after a specified time period to ensure timely completion or expiration.
Set the verification code's TTL to 30 minutes to enforce overall validity. (Time To Live) A pattern where data or tokens have a predefined lifespan after which they are automatically invalidated.

Apply token expiration to enforce the 30-minute validity of the verification code. (Token Expiration) A pattern where tokens used for authentication or verification have an expiration time to limit their validity.

Implement a state machine to track user navigation to bike, scanning/unlocking process, and rental duration management. (State Machine) Manages the states and transitions of the bike rental process, such as bike selection, navigation, scanning/unlocking, and usage timing.

Use observer pattern to notify the user about bike status changes and usage history availability. (Observer) Allows the app to update the biker in real-time about bike availability, location changes, and usage history updates.

Use builder pattern to assemble usage history reports for download. (Builder) Facilitates the construction of complex objects like usage history reports or navigation instructions in a step-by-step manner.

Implement end-to-end encryption for all user data transmissions and storage, including registration and login credentials. (End To End Encryption) Ensures that user data is encrypted from the user's device all the way to the app database, protecting sensitive information during transmission and storage.

Enable login via biometric thumb impression with immediate flushing of biometric data post-authentication to ensure privacy. (Biometric Authentication) Allows users to authenticate using biometric data such as thumb impressions, enhancing security and user convenience.
Implement a 15-minute inactivity timeout to automatically log out users. (Session Timeout) Automatically logs out users after a period of inactivity to prevent unauthorized access from idle sessions.
Provide a logout button that immediately ends the user session. (Logout) Allows users to manually terminate their session by clicking a logout button.

Implement registration form capturing name, email, phone, password, and optional zip code with secure data handling. (User Registration) Enables new users to create an account by providing personal information and credentials.
Implement login via email and password with secure transmission and storage. (Login) Allows users to authenticate using email and password credentials.

Implement a dashboard interface that aggregates bike status and usage data, providing real-time and historical views for the administrator. (Dashboard) A Dashboard pattern provides a centralized visual interface to monitor and analyze key metrics and statuses in real-time.

Use Observer to notify the dashboard or monitoring components about bike status changes in real-time. (Observer) The Observer pattern allows objects (observers) to subscribe to and receive updates from another object (subject) when its state changes.

Use Repository to manage persistence and querying of bike data and usage statistics. (Repository) The Repository pattern abstracts data access, providing a collection-like interface for accessing domain objects.

Implement a scheduler to track rental durations and trigger notifications X minutes before expiry, as well as to calculate overtime charges. (Scheduler) Manages and triggers actions based on time or scheduled events.

Use observer to notify UI or other components when rental state changes, but requires a scheduler or timer to trigger notifications. (Observer) Defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified and updated automatically.

Use state pattern to manage rental lifecycle states but requires scheduler for timing notifications. (State) Allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes, appearing to change its class.
Use strategy to handle different rental pricing calculations but not for notification timing. (Strategy) Defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable.

Use command pattern for encapsulating rental operations but not for scheduling notifications. (Command) Encapsulates a request as an object, thereby allowing for parameterization and queuing of requests.
